title: mantaNets
description: The netlist emitted by 'manta link' (Manta specification revision 1.0, section 15.4).

version.description: The language revision this netlist targets.

top.description: The name of the top-level block the design was elaborated from.

designator.description: The assigned designator, or the path-derived identity when the design is not yet annotated (section 13.1).

path.description: The instance path from the top-level block. Export flattens it (section 13.4).

fitted.description: False for a do-not-populate part. Affects BOM and ERC only; the netlist is unchanged (section 16.3).

type.description: What the part is, from '@type' (section 9.5). Five values are structural -- board_part, boardconnector, cableconnector, wire, crimp -- and the rest are ordinary classifications carried through untouched. Absent means board_part.

section.description: Schematic sheet section, for 'manta render'. Absent when unassigned.

fields.description: User fields, carried through untouched (section 9.1). Values are rendered per section 14.7.

pins.description: Every declared pin in declaration order, connected or not (revision 1.3). The net side carries only connected pins, so this is where NC and unconnected pins survive. Optional: a netlist written before it existed has no such key.

name.description: The logical name the part declares.

direction.description: Absent when the pin carries no arrow.

name.description: The explicit name where one was written, else the name of the first pin on the net (section 5.2).

logical.description: The name the part declares for that pin. Section 15.4's example shows a physical number for one component and a logical name for another; both are emitted so a consumer can take whichever it needs.

type.description: The pin type in force after the strength ladder (section 11.6). Optional: a netlist written before it was emitted simply has no such key, and the reader's default is PASSIVE.

direction.description: The direction the part's arrow declares (section 10). Optional, defaulting to 'none'.

directives.description: Every directive in force on the net, after the strength ladder and any net class have been applied (sections 11.1, 11.9).

blocks.description: Child block instances, in elaboration order, so a renderer can reconstruct the hierarchy the flat netlist came from (revision 1.3). The top block is the design itself and has no entry; absent when there are none, as for a cable.

path.description: The instance path from the top-level block.

block.description: The name of the block definition this instantiates.

section.description: Schematic sheet section, for 'manta render'. Absent when unassigned.

ports.description: The block's declared ports in declaration order, each resolved to the net it reached in this instance.

net.description: Index into 'nets', or -1 when the port reached no emitted net.

localNets.description: Every named net local to this instance -- its local spelling -- mapped to the design net index, sorted by name.

src.description: The reference designator the group is measured from.

tolerance.description: A time, never a length (section 11.4, error E-18). A comma-separated list gives each destination its own budget, which is how a flyby chain is expressed.

offset.description: Required delay relative to the reference. Positive means later.

contains.description: Nested groups. For an outer group, the delay of an inner one is the delay of its reference member.

swaps.description: Pin swaps performed during layout, for 'manta annotate --swaps' to reconcile (section 13.6). Optional: section 15.5 gives the annotator no other input to read them from, so this is a documented extension. See docs/assumptions.md, B2.
